source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Corvette Body, p.1B-32

procedures.title: Fractured panels
steps: Grind or file away all cracked and splintered material from the fracture.
Bevel the fracture edge to roughly 20 degrees.
Strip paint around the fracture with Lacquer Solvent or equivalent.
Scuff the surface for bonding, then clean with Prep-Sol and wipe dry.
Mask adjoining panels with non-staining tape.
Cut a fiberglass cloth strip big enough to overlap the fracture by 1 to 2 inches all around.
Mix the plastic in an unwaxed paper cup (see the Resin Repair Kit procedure).
Wet the glass cloth in the mix by brushing or dipping, then squeeze out the excess.
Lay the wetted cloth over the fracture on the outside of the panel, overlapping 1 to 2 inches, and press it into the break.
Sponge excess plastic out of the cloth, working from the middle of the break toward the edges.
Cut off excess or loose glass strands from the patch.
If there are low spots, mix another batch of resin and hardener thoroughly and add short fibers cut from glass cloth until it is like putty.
Spread the mix generously over the fracture and surrounding area with a spatula, building up enough to allow filing and sanding.
notes: Used when the panel underside cannot be reached or its contour makes back plies impractical.
Avoid resin-rich spots in the cloth: patch strength depends directly on its glass content.
Hold the woven glass in place with Saranwrap or similar until the resin gels.
